searchText: do you guys think in the far future any erc20 token can have a larger marketcap than ethereum itself I highly, highly doubt it. If you take a look at BSC instead of ETH; SafeMoon absolutely skyrocketed the last month (not counting the last week). But even at their peak, they were tiny compared to the network they were on. ETH is much more established, but I don’t think the parent network can ever be flipped. It wouldn’t make sense, since you trade into the token thru the network token. (*don’t kill me for mentioning BSC lol*) Delete it now! 😂 jk It’s just a perfect example Even with an absolutely skyrocketing token, the native network token kinda outpaces the non-native token, since you have to trade thru the network. Granted, I guess if there were a method to go fiat -> non-native token, and the fiat on-ramp was thru a stable coin or even directly into the non-native token, it *could* happen. But that would basically mean some CEX got bigger than Binance, which I don’t foresee. I think instead of using analogies you should stick to mechanisms Token pays fees to parent network for every transfer and contract execution Very true, that’s a good point that I forgot to mention. What use case could grow large enough to capture more value than network while minimizing transfers and execution And yet still remain on network Cause sure it could start as a token and then build out its own chain or whatever future infrastructure is possible Assuming blockchains as we know them innovate Though I suppose if all transactions moved to Layer 2... You could minimize layer 1 fees dramatically And then i suppose the application layer will dwarf the network volume 🤔
